nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a group and $S = (s_1, \dots, s_k)$ a family of $k$ elements generating $\Gamma$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\beta_S(n)$ be the number of elements of $\Gamma$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. The growth rate of $\Gamma$ with respect to $S$ is the real number $\omega(\Gamma, S) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \beta_S(n)^{1/n}$.
nodes.title: Growth rate of a $k$-element generating family (Kourovka 14.7)

nodes.summary: For a group $\Gamma$ generated by a family $S$ of $k$ elements and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\beta_S(n)$ be the number of elements of $\Gamma$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$, and let $\omega(\Gamma, S) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \beta_S(n)^{1/n}$ be the growth rate. nodes.title: Amenable groups with growth rate close to $2k - 1$ (Kourovka 15.4 refuted)

nodes.summary: The proposition, asked by P. de la Harpe, that there are $k \ge 2$ and a real $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every group $\Gamma$ generated by a family $S$ of $k$ distinct elements whose growth rate satisfies $\omega(\Gamma, S) \ge 2k - 1 - \varepsilon$ is non-amenable (amenability being the Følner condition).
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 15.4 (large growth rate implies non-amenability)
